units.note: The gnomic lines are terse; the English is a defensible reading.

findings.quote: pretended that he was going aboard for the voyage and slipped away
findings.problem: The Greek is προσποιηθεὶς ὡς ἐπιναύσιος γεγονὼς ἀπηλλάττετο. ἐπιναύσιος means nauseated or sick, so Demetrius pretended to be sick (from the drinking) and left. Nothing in the Greek says he was going aboard.
findings.proposed_fix: pretended to be sick with nausea and took his leave

findings.quote: This was why they appointed Tiberius, because he had been an eyewitness of the whole situation.
findings.problem: The Greek is διὸ τὸν Τεβέριον κατεστήσαντο *** πάντων αὐτόπτην γεγονέναι. The *** marks a lacuna between κατεστήσαντο and πάντων. The English reads on as if the sentence were whole, and it invents a causal 'because' clause.
findings.proposed_fix: This was why they appointed Tiberius [text missing] to have been an eyewitness of everything.

units.note: The final fragment (ὁ δὲ Δημήτριος προσανέχων τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ διαποσταλησομένου πρὸς αὐτόν) is an excerpt-ending and incomplete in the Greek. The English is acceptable.

findings.quote: The finest quality of any letter is its power to establish goodwill.
findings.problem: The Greek is ὅτι παντὸς ἐπιστολίου τὸ κάλλος ἐστὶ συστατικώτερον. The subject is τὸ κάλλος (beauty, or good looks) and the comparison is with παντὸς ἐπιστολίου (than any letter). So beauty is a stronger recommendation than any letter of introduction. The English inverts the sense and makes the letter the subject.
findings.proposed_fix: Beauty is a stronger recommendation than any letter of introduction.

units.note: The gap after ἐπανελέσθαι is already marked [text missing] in the English. The verb ἐπανελέσθαι is itself uncertain in sense, so it was not touched. The second excerpt is a bare fragment.
The text at ἐπὶ Μοχυρίνου looks possibly corrupt, and the English handles it neutrally.

findings.quote: he nevertheless left his private fortune in such a state that his family could not repay
findings.problem: The Greek is τοσοῦτον ἀπέλειπε τὸν ἴδιον βίον ὥστε * ** μὴ δύνασθαι τὴν φερνὴν. It has a lacuna of a few words after ὥστε, before μὴ δύνασθαι. The English reads straight on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: he nevertheless left his private fortune in such a state that [text missing] his family could not repay

units.note: The subject of δύνασθαι is lost in the gap, so 'his family' is an inference.
